Growing Healthy Tomatoes Choose the Right Variety Plan the Planting Time Select the Location Harden Off Seedlings Pruning Harvesting
Select tomato seeds based on your climate, soil type, and intended use (e.g., cherry tomatoes, heirloom, or Roma). Consider disease-resistant varieties for a healthier crop. Tomatoes thrive in warm weather. Plan to plant after the last frost date in your region. Use a calendar to ensure your seedlings are ready for transplanting. Choose a location with full sun (at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily). Ensure good air circulation to prevent fungal diseases. 1. Dig a hole twice as wide and slightly deeper than the seedling\'s root ball.\n\n2. Plant deeply - bury the stem up to the first set of leaves to encourage strong root development.\n\n3. Space plants 18-24 inches apart.\n\n4. Water thoroughly after planting. 1. Remove small shoots growing between the main stem and branches to focus energy on fruit production.\n\n2. Prune lower leaves to prevent disease spread from the soil. 1. Tomatoes are ready to harvest when they are firm, fully colored, and slightly soft to the touch.\n\n2. Gently twist or cut the fruit from the plant to avoid damage.\n\n3. Harvest regularly to encourage continued fruit production.

Choose high-quality onion seeds that are suited to your climate and soil conditions. Opt for certified seeds for better results. Prepare the soil by loosening it to improve aeration. Add organic compost and ensure the soil has good drainage to prevent waterlogging. Plant onion seeds or seedlings in rows, leaving enough space between them to allow for growth. Ensure they are planted at the appropriate depth. Water the onions regularly, especially during dry periods. Avoid overwatering, as onions prefer moist but not soggy soil. Harvest onions when the tops turn yellow and start to fall over. Cure the onions in a dry, well-ventilated area for better storage.
